newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden blames EU for killing of stressed turtles.
newsitem.headline: Sweden blames EU for killing of stressed turtles.

text.p: Some 1,000 stressed Russian turtles are in the soup in Sweden, doomed by EU regulations.
Farm officials said on Thursday that 1,000 sick turtles detected by customs officers would have to be destroyed because of rules laid down by Brussels.
Sweden's Agricultural authority, Jordburksverket, said in a statement the turtles had come from Russia but were too ill to be returned there.
Many had died since they arrived and most were too stressed by their experience to eat. "All the turtles are in a bad way and it is considered impossible to return them to Russia."
Sweden had applied for an exception to European Union rules which bar the importation of endangered species.
"The application was rejected and all other 14 EU countries have been told not to take care of the turtles."
"It is tragic that we have to kill the turtles but there is unfortunately no other possibility," said Bengt Nordblom, head of the agricultural authority's animal division.
"The turtles cannot be brought into Sweden and it is not possible to send them back," he added.
